svg.title: Gold PUBLISHED Stage A — in-sample vs-flat-DCA keep/drop (NOT vs-lump, NOT Sharpe)
svg.desc: IN-SAMPLE, and a SELECTED UPPER BOUND. Every in-sample figure is the MAXIMUM over the shipped frozen weight grid, scored against the same in-sample folds it was fitted on. This chart is NOT a performance claim and NOT a validated result: no return, Sharpe or edge is asserted beyond the metrics the shipped search returned. OOS is printed for information only — nothing was selected on it.
svg.text: Gold PUBLISHED Stage A — in-sample vs-flat-DCA keep/drop (NOT vs-lump, NOT Sharpe)
GLD-USD · objective: mean IN-SAMPLE vs_flat_dca_pct · floor 10% deployed, cap 50% drawdown · curve gold_reselect · rails rolling_z 90d/z1.0
4 PANELS — keep/drop, the two rails, then OOS BELOW A RULE — plus the shape comparison
JOINT SWEEP searched 6 of 13 allowlist names in 2,186 evaluations on the SHIPPED frozen grids. FEASIBILITY CALL: the full allowlist projects to
4,782,969 evaluations at the measured 33.0 ms/eval = 43.8 h, which does not fit a session. The narrowing is a COVERAGE budget, a data property, never
THE OBJECTIVE CONSUMES NO CYCLE WINDOWS — it cuts its own folds from the calendar, so this is ONE run, and the gold pin sets are not an input. The
preceding diagnostic scored cycle-window overlap instead: a DIFFERENT OBJECTIVE, and the two results must not be blended into a single claim.
IMPORTANT: the shipped Stage A rank does NOT gate on the floor or the cap. The frozen objective records the feasibility flag per fold and Stage B
enforces it, but the Stage A argmax is the plain mean in-sample vs_flat_dca_pct. Nothing here may claim a row was vetoed for breaching the floor or
the cap. Read the feasibility flag as recorded fact, not as a filter that ran.
OUT-OF-SAMPLE IS VOID IN THIS RUN — every OOS window deployed zero capital, so every OOS figure is the same all-cash book. The shipped no-trend
rolling-z rails are refit per fold on the in-sample window, and RollingZRiskModel.rails() left-joins a stored history, so every later date returns
null rails, null risk and no trades. A trend rail would extrapolate; this one cannot. In-sample panels are unaffected. Panel 4 says so at the point of
1 · KEEP / NO-KEEP PER EXTRA — in-sample vs-flat-DCA, against the valuation-only baseline (bar RIGHT = the leg beat it)
✓ keep · in joint sweep · worst window 1.7% (fold0_is)
✓ keep · in joint sweep · worst window 1.8% (fold0_is)
✓ keep · in joint sweep · worst window 1.7% (fold0_is)
✓ keep · in joint sweep · worst window 5.7% (fold0_is)
✓ keep · in joint sweep · worst window 11.0% (fold0_is)
✓ keep · in joint sweep · worst window 2.6% (fold0_is)
NO-KEEP IS NOT A DROP. A one-name sweep shares its grid with the valuation-only row, so its best can never fall below the baseline: a leg that
actively hurts and a leg that merely does not help are the same observation here, and both read as 'no keep earned'. For whether the joint winner
actually carries a leg, read panel 5.
2 · DEPLOYED CAPITAL vs THE 10% FLOOR — peak-deployed share per fold, on the joint-sweep winner
feasible flag True (recorded, not enforced at Stage A)
feasible flag True (recorded, not enforced at Stage A)
feasible flag True (recorded, not enforced at Stage A)
The 10% floor is a RAIL to read against, not a filter that ran: the shipped Stage A rank is the plain mean in-sample vs_flat_dca_pct and does not gate
on it. A fold left of the rail is a recorded fact, not a vetoed row.
3 · DRAWDOWN vs THE 50% CAP — per fold, on the joint-sweep winner
The 50% cap is likewise a rail, not a Stage A filter. Both rails are drawn because the objective is DEFINED with them, and they are drawn because a
reader should be able to see the margin — not because any row was rejected for crossing one.
5 · THE WINNER'S SHAPE vs the published btc_sdca reference — shape comparison only, not a tuning target
gold joint-sweep winner: valuation 0.5 + weekly_rsi 1, weekly_macd 1
published btc_sdca reference: valuation 1, m2 0.5, dxy 0.5, weekly_macd 0.5, weekly_rsi 0.25
legs: gold 3 vs btc_sdca 5 · partial-weight legs: gold 0 vs btc_sdca 4 (0.5 / 0.5 / 0.5 / 0.25)
The reference is the precedent for what a real multi-leg composite looks like. It is reported here for shape only: nothing was copied from it, tuned
toward it, or benchmarked against it.
OUT-OF-SAMPLE — REPORTED, NEVER USED FOR SELECTION
*** VOID — every window below deployed ZERO capital, so these bars are one all-cash book repeated ***
THIS PANEL IS VOID AND THE BARS MUST NOT BE READ AS EVIDENCE. Every out-of-sample window in this run deployed zero capital: the shipped no-trend
rolling-z rails are refit on each fold's in-sample window, and RollingZRiskModel.rails() left-joins a stored (date, mu, sigma) table, so every date
outside that fit window comes back null. Null rails give null risk, null risk gives no trades, and the fold is all cash. A trend rail would
extrapolate and this would not. The in-sample panels above are unaffected — in-sample dates are inside the fit window. Stage B must score these folds
through the concatenated-history rolling loop the gold curve search already carries, or use rails that extrapolate.
BARS LENGTH = the change in in-sample vs_flat_dCA_pct against the valuation-only baseline, on the same folds. A leg that cannot beat valuation-only
alone reads as 'no keep' — not as a drop, because a one-name sweep shares its grid with the baseline row and so can never score below it.
THE RAILS DID NOT GATE. The 10% floor and the 50% cap define the objective and are drawn so the margin is visible, but the shipped Stage A rank is
the plain mean in-sample vs_flat_dCA_pct and vetoes nothing. The per-fold feasible flag is recorded, not enforced.
OOS IS IN ITS OWN PANEL BELOW A RULE because it was reported and never used to select. Nothing on this figure was chosen by an out-of-sample number.
FEASIBILITY: 6 of 13 names in the joint sweep; every excluded name is named with its measured coverage in the console and the JSON, and every
allowlist name still carries a single-leg probe row — so no name is silently absent.
NO GOLD PROFILE EXISTS in asset_profile.py; this run builds one from the module's own public surface and edits no source file. The rails are the
shipped no-trend rolling-z anchor; the curve is the shipped gold_reselect preset resolved by name. No power-law and no generic log-linear /
log-quadratic steer for gold appears anywhere.
IN-SAMPLE, and a SELECTED UPPER BOUND. Every in-sample figure is the MAXIMUM over the shipped frozen weight grid, scored against the same in-sample
folds it was fitted on. This chart is NOT a performance claim and NOT a validated result: no return, Sharpe or edge is asserted beyond the metrics the
shipped search returned. OOS is printed for information only — nothing was selected on it.
held out of the joint sweep: uup, gvz, walcl, hy_oas, ig_oas, gdx_gld, gld_slv
